notes.r-p6-01:0: Insertion, key C (only one elevator shut at a time). Near-correct A 'Both elevators will therefore be out of service until March 20' follows 'The work is expected to take five days' perfectly and 'therefore' makes it look like the natural conclusion. Deciding clue is in P2: 'the elevator that remains in service' and 'leave it free'. B (dates not yet set) is killed by P1 sentence 1 and the subject line; D (loading dock closed) by P2/P3. Self band hard (L D B).
notes.r-p6-01:1: Pronoun, key A it. Near-correct B them: pulled by the nearest plural 'the stairs' and by 'two passenger elevators' in P1; C one ('leave one free') is a real pattern but needs two or more running. Deciding clue: singular 'the elevator that remains in service' in the previous sentence plus P1's 'only one at a time'. Self band hard (L D B S).
notes.r-p6-01:2: Tense, key B will be. Near-correct A has been ('has been open to tenants each weekday' reads fine alone). Deciding clue: e-mail dated March 9, work starts March 16 (P1), 'During the work ... will be' in P2, and 'normally used only by building staff' in the same sentence. Self band medium (L D; B no).
notes.r-p6-01:3: Connector/conditional, key D unless. Near-correct A even if ('postpone them even if ...' is natural if the building took no deliveries at all); C although fails the same way. Deciding clue in P2: the freight elevator 'will be open to tenants for deliveries from 6 to 8 a.m.'; 'during those hours' must also be traced back to P2. Self band hard (L D B S).
notes.r-p6-02:0: Linking adverb, key D As a result. Near-correct A Nevertheless, helped by the negative word 'rejected' in the previous sentence. Deciding clue: 'far fewer rejected claims than they had with the paper forms' is a good result, so the switch follows from it. Otherwise / For example fail on meaning. Self band hard (L D B); the clue is the adjacent sentence, so the blind review may call it medium.
notes.r-p6-02:1: Adverb, key B still. Near-correct A no longer: after 'receipts are simply photographed ... and attached', 'no longer need to keep the originals' is the natural guess. Deciding clue is the next sentence: 'Our auditors may ask to see them' (them = the original receipts). Self band hard (L D B).
notes.r-p6-02:2: Insertion, key A ('This earlier date lets us repay claims in the month they are submitted'). Near-correct C 'Claims that arrive after that date will no longer be accepted' (a common rule, fits right after 'must be submitted by the 5th') is contradicted by the next sentence (late claims are repaid the following month). B 'This later date' needs the 15th-vs-5th comparison; D (paper accepted until year end) contradicts P1 'replace the paper forms ... starting October 1'. Self band hard (L D S).
notes.r-p6-02:3: Participle, key C submitted. Near-correct B are submitted: 'Claims are submitted after the 5th' is a full sentence until 'will be repaid' shows the main verb is already there. Clue is in-sentence, so D is no for Part 6. Self band medium (L B).
notes.r-p6-03:0: Insertion, key B ('Expanding the original bakery, however, was never an option'), explained by the next sentence (narrow lot). Near-correct A 'The company plans to close the Mill Road bakery once the new site opens': the narrow-lot sentence reads like the reason for closing. Deciding clue in P3 (Mill Road will concentrate on bread and keep baking some pastries) and P4 (no one has to move). C (two sites for years) contradicts P1 'Until now, everything ... at its original bakery'; D (ovens off at night) contradicts 'around the clock'. Self band hard (L D B).
notes.r-p6-03:1: Tense, key D began. Near-correct A will begin: 'will begin in March, and ... is due to open in October' is consistent inside the sentence. Only the dateline (June 12) and 'this autumn' in P1 rule it out. B has begun is the Taiwanese-learner trap (present perfect with 'in March'). Self band hard (L D B S).
notes.r-p6-03:2: Conjunction, key C Until. Near-correct A Once ('Once the new site is running at full capacity' is the stock phrase in such articles). Deciding clue: the previous sentence's plan that the new site takes over ALL pastry production, so Mill Road can keep some pastries only before full capacity. Even though contradicts the October opening; In case is nonsense. Self band hard (L D B).
notes.r-p6-03:3: Vocabulary, key A opportunity. Near-correct B obligation (and C instruction): 'be given the obligation to transfer' reads fine alone. Deciding clue: previous sentence 'no current employee will be required to move'. Plain meaning contrast, so B no. Self band medium (L D).
notes.r-p6-04:0: Preposition, key A Unlike. Near-correct B Like: 'Like the printed magazine, the digital edition will reach you on the first of every month' is grammatical and sounds reassuring. Deciding clue in P1: the printed copy 'often arrives a week or more after the first of the month'. Despite / Except for fail on meaning. Self band hard (L D S).
notes.r-p6-04:1: Insertion, key C ('The new rate will apply to all subscriptions, including renewals'). Near-correct A 'Readers who have already renewed, however, will keep paying the old rate' is a common rule and fits right after the price cut; the next sentence (refund of the difference) kills it. D '$96 print price' is killed only by P3 ($72 + extra $30 = $102). B 'first price increase' contradicts the fall from $96 to $72. Self band hard (L D B S).
notes.r-p6-04:2: Relative pronoun, key D who. Near-correct A whom: 'our records' right after the blank looks like the subject, so the blank looks like an object; remove 'our records show' and the blank is the subject of 'have paid' (hypercorrection trap). Clue is in-sentence. Self band medium (L B S).
notes.r-p6-04:3: Conditional inversion, key B Should. Near-correct A Would: 'Would you prefer to keep receiving the magazine by mail' reads as a polite question until the comma and the imperative 'please check'. Had needs a past participle and a past counterfactual; Were needs 'Were you to'. Clue is in-sentence. Self band medium (L B).
